processing: Little is documented about this tea specifically; as with other Chinese gongfu blacks it should be withered, rolled, fully oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: Not well documented; spring picking is usually the most prized in Hubei black teas.
appearance_dry: As is typical of Chinese gongfu blacks, thin dark twisted strands.
appearance_liquor: As is typical of the class, a clear orange-red.
appearance_wet: As is typical of the class, soft reddish-brown leaf.
taste_profile: No reliable tasting description is on record; expect the sweet, malty profile usual for Hubei gongfu black teas.

brewing.notes: Standard settings for a Chinese gongfu black, since nothing specific to this tea is recorded. Adjust by taste.

vintage_note: No special vintage practice is documented. As usual for gongfu black teas, look for the current or previous year's harvest and check the producer and picking date.
description:
Badong Hong is a black tea from Badong county in the Three Gorges part of western Hubei, within Enshi prefecture. The name is closely linked with a recent company venture, so it may be better understood as a young local tea than as a long-standing appellation.

Little is documented about how it is made. It should follow the usual gongfu black method of withering, rolling, oxidation and drying, and the taste should sit near other Hubei blacks: sweet and malty, but that is a guess from the class rather than a fact about this tea.

If you find some, ask who made it and when it was picked, and brew it like any Chinese gongfu black: short steeps, hot water, and see what is there.
history:
Badong has an old tea reputation: local accounts claim tribute tea from the early Western Zhou, which is hard to verify, and the county is linked with the tea-road trade of the Three Gorges. Its favoured local variety is Badong big-leaf tea.

The black tea itself is much harder to trace. A company named Hubei Zhengshantang Badong Hong Tea set up a raw-leaf base in the county with long contracts for growers. When the name first appeared is not documented.
